title: CorrectBench: Automatic Testbench Generation with Functional Self-Correction using LLMs for HDL Design
problem: LLM-based hardware testbench generation produces functional errors without automatic correction mechanisms; performance is especially poor for sequential circuit testing.
motivation: Manual HDL testbench generation is time-consuming; LLM-based automation is promising but suffers from correctness issues limiting practical adoption.
method: CorrectBench framework uses LLM to generate testbenches from RTL specification, performs automatic functional validation, and applies self-correction using bug information from validation failures; iteratively improves until passing.
key_novelty: Automatic functional self-correction mechanism that uses bug information to fix generated testbenches without human intervention.
contributions: Self-correction improving overall pass rate to 70.13% vs 52.18% prior work
62.18% improvement for sequential circuits over previous method
baselines: Prior LLM-based testbench generation (52.18% pass rate)
primary_theme: LLM-based HDL testbench generation with self-correction
